description: The figure presents three pie charts comparing the distribution of four labeled categories across difficulty settings (“easy,” “medium,” and a third chart at right), with each chart divided into 4 slices. In the “easy” chart, the slices are labeled by color as teal (55.4%), yellow (38.3%), light orange (4.6%), and red-orange (1.7%), with percentage values printed inside the slices. In the “medium” chart, the teal slice is 58.8%, the yellow slice is 35.4%, the light orange slice is 4.0%, and the red-orange slice is 1.8%, again with percentages shown inside. In the rightmost chart, the light orange slice is 37.9%, the yellow slice is 37.3%, the teal slice is 18.1%, and the red-orange slice is 6.7%, with internal percentage labels. A legend appears to the right mapping the four colors to category labels (readable as variants of N/K sign combinations), and none of the slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized; the slice sizes appear arranged by their angular spans rather than a clearly consistent ordering across all three pies.
